page: Microsoft Azure E96s_v5 is a high-capacity memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is built on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock of 2.8 GHz. It provides 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 48 physical processor cores with two threads per core. System memory totals 672 GB, providing a memory density of 7.0 GB per vCPU. Instruction set capabilities include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and hardware-accelerated cryptographic processing through AES, VAES, and SHA extensions. The instance carries no integrated local ephemeral or NVMe storage and includes no GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached remote storage.

Benchmark results place the multi-core processing capabilities and memory throughput of the E96s_v5 in the top twenty-five percent of measured cloud instances. Multi-core execution scores high in stress-ng and Geekbench, driven by parallel scaling across its 96 vCPUs. Memory bandwidth benchmarks demonstrate uncached read rates of 322.18 GB/sec and cached small-block throughput exceeding 5000 GB/sec. Cryptographic evaluation places the system in the top tier, supported by native instruction extensions. Conversely, single-core processing tests across Geekbench and stress-ng fall into median ranges, indicating that performance gains derive from parallel scaling rather than raw single-thread clock speed.

In terms of qualitative efficiency, the instance provides significant resource consolidation for workloads requiring expansive memory footprints and parallel compute without paying for unused GPU silicon. Because local storage is absent, storage performance and expenditure remain dependent on attached remote disk tiers, which adds architectural flexibility but requires appropriate disk provisioning to match system throughput. For large language model workloads, CPU inference demonstrates usable prompt ingestion on smaller models but exhibits weak token generation on larger architectures.

The E96s_v5 is best suited for large-scale in-memory databases such as Redis, enterprise relational database management systems, multi-threaded batch compilation, and memory-heavy data analytics pipelines. Its high core density and extensive RAM make it effective for consolidated container environments and enterprise transactional workloads.
description: The Microsoft Azure E96s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores and 672 GB of system memory, the instance delivers an allocation of 7.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX-512 vector extensions, AVX-512 VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI. The instance contains no bundled local disk storage, requiring network-attached remote volumes for persistent data. Benchmark assessments indicate average single-core CPU throughput balanced by top-quartile multi-core execution and high memory read bandwidth reaching 322.18 GB/sec. Cryptographic performance ranks in the top ten percent, alongside solid capabilities in database operations and static web serving throughput. Due to its balanced memory density and high core count, the E96s_v5 fits enterprise in-memory databases, Redis caches, big data analytics, and large multi-threaded batch processing pipelines.
